## Purpose and entry points
Claude Code Haha is a cross-platform local AI coding workbench built around a Claude-Code-derived CLI/runtime, with a React desktop UI, local API server, remote/IM access, and agent tooling. Primary entry points are the Bun CLI launcher (`bin/claude-haha`, `src/entrypoints/cli.tsx`), terminal application (`src/main.tsx`, `src/screens/REPL.tsx`), local server (`src/server/index.ts`, `src/server/server.ts`), and desktop renderer/main processes (`desktop/src/main.tsx`, `desktop/electron/main.ts`).

## Agent execution core
The CLI runtime owns interactive sessions, prompt handling, streaming model queries, state, and terminal rendering. User input is routed through command/text processors into the query engine; streamed model events create messages, invoke tools, request approval, and update persisted session state. Key boundaries: UI-facing React/Ink code vs. model/tool orchestration and filesystem/process effects.
- `src/QueryEngine.ts`
- `src/query.ts`
- `src/services/tools/toolOrchestration.ts`

## Tool, permission, and multi-agent layer
Tools implement code edits, file/search access, shell execution, MCP, browser/computer use, scheduled tasks, and subagents. Permission modes and rules gate consequential execution; UI approval handlers bridge decisions back into tool runs. Agent/Team tasks can run in-process, shell-backed, or remote contexts and report progress through task abstractions.
- `src/tools/AgentTool/AgentTool.tsx`
- `src/utils/permissions/permissions.ts`
- `src/tasks/LocalAgentTask/LocalAgentTask.tsx`

## Local server and desktop API boundary
The desktop application talks to a locally managed server over HTTP/WebSocket rather than importing the CLI runtime directly. Router/API modules expose conversations, sessions, providers, filesystem/workspaces, MCP, tasks, indexing, and diagnostics; services contain persistence and domain operations. WebSocket events carry streaming session and state changes to clients.
- `src/server/router.ts`
- `src/server/api/conversations.ts`
- `src/server/ws/handler.ts`

## Desktop application architecture
The desktop UI is React/Vite stateful workbench: stores call typed API clients, render chat/workspace/settings/activity pages, and consume WebSocket updates. Electron owns privileged native capabilities—window lifecycle, IPC capability checks, keychain, notifications, shell/terminal, updater, and lifecycle of the local server/sidecar. A Tauri implementation also exists under `desktop/src-tauri`, indicating an alternate/native packaging path.
- `desktop/src/App.tsx`
- `desktop/src/stores/sessionStore.ts`
- `desktop/electron/services/serverRuntime.ts`

## Persistence, workspace, and search
Local services manage session transcripts, workspace/project launching, settings, task schedules, and local indexes. The local-index subsystem maintains databases, migrations, projections, reconciliation, and searchable session/content/activity/trace views. This separates durable/queryable desktop state from live CLI session execution.
- `src/server/services/sessionService.ts`
- `src/server/services/localIndex/coordinator.ts`
- `src/server/services/workspaceService.ts`

## External integrations and delivery channels
Model access supports Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI-style provider transformations, official OAuth flows, and provider runtime environments. MCP and LSP extend tools and editor intelligence. Remote access includes H5 policy/auth and bridge sessions; IM adapters normalize Telegram, Feishu, WeChat, DingTalk, and WhatsApp messages, attachments, streaming output, sessions, and permission interactions.
- `src/server/proxy/handler.ts`
- `src/services/mcp/MCPConnectionManager.tsx`
- `adapters/common/ws-bridge.ts`

## Runtime and infrastructure
Core code is TypeScript running primarily on Bun; terminal UI uses React/Ink; desktop uses Electron plus React/Vite, with Rust/Tauri assets also present. Native helpers support computer-use/runtime tasks via Python (`runtime/requirements.txt`). Releases build desktop packages for macOS, Windows, and Linux through GitHub Actions.
- `package.json`
- `desktop/package.json`
- `.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml`
